title: Check Good Integer
summary: Given a positive integer n, calculate the sum of its digits (digitSum) and the sum of the squares of its digits (squareSum).
statement: Given a positive integer n, calculate the sum of its digits (digitSum) and the sum of the squares of its digits (squareSum). Determine if n is good by checking if squareSum minus digitSum is at least 50. Return true if n is good, otherwise return false.
constraints: Let digitSum be the sum of decimal digits and squareSum their squared sum.
n is good when squareSum-digitSum is at least fifty.
reference_solution:
def is_good_digit_integer(n):
    return sum(int(digit)*(int(digit)-1) for digit in str(n))>=50
hints: For a digit d, its contribution is d squared minus d.
Compute d*(d-1) for each decimal digit.
Sum the contributions and compare with fifty inclusively.

tests.explanation: Both sums are one, so their difference is zero and the result is false.
The difference is 82 minus 10, which is seventy-two and passes.
